title: dev.qory.run.started
description: The run is open: with opened_by session the runtime is about to start; with opened_by gateway a gateway opened the run on a run credential, and no runtime starts. The first event of a run in the file, and the event a receiver creates the run on.

opened_by.description: What opened the run. session: a Forager session around a runtime, which emits this event as the runtime is about to start, with runtime, command, args, dir and interactive. gateway: a gateway, on a run credential a client presented through its proxy, with no session; the run has no process, so this event contains none of runtime, runtime_version, command, args, dir, interactive, terminal, host, wall and image, and its dev.qory.run.exited contains no exit_code.

credential.description: Where the run's credential came from. starter: the run's starter gave the run its run credential, as for a session's run on a gateway's one address and every run a gateway opened. none: the run has no run credential, as for a run on a gateway's local link. The gateway decides it, and a session copies it from the gateway's run answer. Nothing else of the starter is reported.

runtime_version.description: The runtime version Forager's adapter for it, such as a descriptor, was written against; Forager never checks the installed version. Absent for a bare runtime, whose records the session does not parse, and when the runtime's adapter reports no version.

command.description: The program started, as the runtime prepared it.

args.description: Its arguments, as the runtime prepared them. Environment is never reported.

dir.description: The working directory the runtime starts in.

interactive.description: True when the session runs on a pseudo-terminal, false on pipes.

terminal.description: The size of the pseudo-terminal the runtime starts on: Forager's own terminal's when it has one, 80 by 24 otherwise. Present when interactive is true, absent on pipes. Every change after that is one dev.qory.run.resized.

forager_version.description: The version of the Forager that opened the run: the session's, or the gateway's for a run a gateway opened.

host.description: The host name of the agent's machine, the one the runtime runs on.

wall.description: The adapter that built the enclosure the runtime runs in: docker. Absent when there is no wall, where command and dir are the machine's own; present, they are the enclosure's.

image.description: The image the enclosure runs, the reference. Present with wall.

image_name.description: The machine's name for the image, when the image is one the machine defines: the one the policy selected, or the machine's default by name.

container_runtime.description: The container runtime the wall started the image under, as the machine's definition sets it: sysbox-runc. Absent means the engine's default.

docker.description: True when the enclosure has a Docker daemon of its own, started by the wall before the runtime. Absent otherwise.

labels.description: The caller's own names for the run, its key in a queue, a repository, an issue, as the command that started the run received them, or, for a run a gateway opened, as the run credential's mapping gives them, run_key among them. Forager copies them and reads nothing into them. Only this event contains them among the events, and the gateway's registration of the run sends them in its body, never in a URL; a receiver keeps them with the run it creates on it.

about.description: What the run is about, as the caller passed it, or, for a run a gateway opened, details as the run credential's mapping gives them: the kind of run, a title, the subjects it works on and details, every member optional. Forager copies it and reads nothing into it. Only this event contains it among the events, and the gateway's registration of the run sends it in its body; it never selects or changes a security policy. An empty about is left out. No string in it, key or value, contains a control character: U+0000 to U+001F, U+007F to U+009F, U+2028 and U+2029. Forager alone checks these rules, which the schema cannot state: the byte limits, the 8192 bytes of details, that no two subjects have the same type and ref, a url's syntax and host, that a url carries no user name or password, and that no member name appears twice in details. Each maxLength counts characters and is an upper bound of the byte limit the description states.

kind.description: The kind of run, the caller's word, at most 64 bytes.

title.description: The run's title, at most 256 bytes.

subjects.description: What the run works on, 1 to 16. No two subjects have the same type and ref: a subject is identified by its type and ref.

type.description: The subject's type, an open name the caller chooses: words of a-z and 0-9, each joined to the next by one space, underscore, dot or dash, at most 64 bytes.

ref.description: The subject's reference, at most 256 bytes.

url.description: Where the subject is shown: an absolute http or https URL, at most 2048 bytes. A url never carries a user name or password.

title.description: The subject's title, at most 256 bytes.

details.description: A JSON object of the caller's, at most 8192 bytes as this event contains it, compacted, with <, > and & written as \u003c, \u003e and \u0026, and nested at most 4 levels deep: details is level 1, and an object or an array inside it is level 2. A key is 1 to 64 bytes. It is shown to every reader of the run, so it never holds a secret.

about_details_1.description: Level 1: details itself, an object of scalars and level 2 objects and arrays.

about_details_2.description: Level 2: an object or an array of scalars and level 3 objects and arrays.

about_details_3.description: Level 3: an object or an array of scalars and level 4 objects and arrays.

about_details_4.description: Level 4, the deepest: an object or an array of scalars only.
